**Netflix Download Limits — How plans differ, devices, and the “2 devices / 15 downloads” rule**

I’ll answer **point-by-point, cleanly**, no marketing fluff.

---

## 1️⃣ Does the Netflix download limit differ by plan?

**Yes. Very clearly.**

Netflix limits **offline downloads** by **plan + number of allowed devices**.

### Typical structure (as of 2025):

| Plan | Devices for downloads | Monthly download limit |
|----|----|----|
| **Basic with Ads** | ❌ Not supported | ❌ No downloads |
| **Basic (no ads)** | 1 device | ~15 downloads / month |
| **Standard** | 2 devices | ~15 downloads **per device / month** |
| **Premium** | 4 devices | ~15 downloads **per device / month** |

> ✔️ The popup you showed  
> **“15 monthly downloads per device for 2 total devices”**  
> = **Standard plan**

📌 **Important:**  
The limit resets **on the 1st of every calendar month**, not 30 days rolling.

---

## 2️⃣ What exactly counts as a “download”?

Netflix counts **each title download**:

- 1 movie = 1 download  
- 1 episode = 1 download  
- Re-downloading the *same title again* = **counts again**
- Deleting and re-downloading = **counts again**

Quality (HD vs SD) **does NOT change the count** — only storage.

---

## 3️⃣ “2 devices” — how does the 15-download limit apply?

This is the key confusion. Let’s make it precise.

### Your plan says:
> **15 downloads per device × 2 devices**

That means:

- 📱 **Mobile 1** → 15 downloads / month  
- 📱 **Mobile 2** → 15 downloads / month  

✅ **Yes — the second mobile gets its own separate 15 downloads**

They do **not share** the same 15.

So total potential = **30 downloads/month**, but split per device.

---

## 4️⃣ Can I download on a laptop?

### ❌ Browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari)
No. Downloads are **not allowed in browsers**.

### ✅ Windows laptop (official Netflix app)
Yes — **only if**:
- Windows 10 or 11
- Netflix app from Microsoft Store

Counts as **one device**.

### ❌ MacBook (macOS)
No offline downloads at all.
Netflix does **not** support downloads on macOS (still true in 2025).

---

## 5️⃣ What devices count toward the limit?

Counted devices include:
- Android phones
- iPhones
- iPads
- Windows laptops (Netflix app only)

Each registered device gets its **own 15-download quota**.

If you remove a device:
- Existing downloads stop working
- The monthly quota **does not transfer**

---

## 6️⃣ Practical advice (to avoid hitting the limit again)

- Download **series episodes selectively**
- Avoid deleting + re-downloading the same title
- Use **one device for long trips**, another for casual viewing
- If you’re close to month-end → **wait for reset on the 1st**

---

## One-line summary

> ✔️ Yes, limits differ by plan  
> ✔️ 15 downloads **per device**, not shared  
> ✔️ Laptop downloads only on **Windows Netflix app**  
> ❌ MacBooks & browsers can’t download  
> 🔁 Limit resets every month on the 1st

If you want, tell me **your exact Netflix plan name**, and I’ll map **your best download strategy** (mobile vs laptop) precisely.

Here’s how **Amazon Prime Video offline downloads** compare — *simple, clear answers like your Netflix question:*

---

## 🎥 1️⃣ Does Amazon Prime Video let you download shows offline?

✅ **Yes.**  
Prime Video lets you download movies/episodes to watch offline in the **Prime Video app** on phones, tablets, and some laptops. It **doesn’t work in a web browser**. citeturn0search10

---

## 📱 2️⃣ How many downloads can you have at once?

📌 There *is a limit*, and it’s different from Netflix:

- On many accounts, you can download **about 15–25 total titles** at once across all your devices.  
  This is a **global account limit**, not per device. citeturn0search15turn0search18

Example:  
If you download 10 movies on your phone and 15 episodes on your tablet, you may have hit the maximum **25 titles total** — even if they’re on different devices. citeturn0search29

📌 This number **varies by region** and content rights, but *most users see 15–25*. citeturn0search24

---

## 🔄 3️⃣ Does it reset monthly?

❌ **No fixed “resets per month” like Netflix.**  
Instead, the limit is **how many you can hold at the same time.** To make space for new ones, you must **delete old downloads** from any device.

---

## 📱💻 4️⃣ How many devices can download at the *same time*?

- You can **download titles on up to *2 devices*** concurrently (for normal Prime subscription content). citeturn0search27

This is different from:
- **Streaming on multiple devices at once** — usually up to 2–3 simultaneous streams is supported on Prime. citeturn0search30

So:
- Phone + Tablet = OK  
- If you already downloaded on 2 devices, you must delete a download from one of them before downloading on a third.

---

## 💻 5️⃣ Can you download on a laptop?

Yes — but only **through the Prime Video app** if your device supports it:

**Supported for downloads:**
- **Windows 10/11 app**
- **Android phones/tablets**
- **iPhone / iPad**
- Some Fire tablets

❌ **Not via web browser.** citeturn0search10

---

## ⏳ 6️⃣ Expiry of downloads

- Usually, offline downloads last **up to ~30 days**.  
- Once you start watching, you typically have **48 hours to finish** before it expires. citeturn0search8

(This is similar to most OTT download rules.)

---

### 📌 Quick Prime Download Summary

| Feature | Amazon Prime Video |
|---------|--------------------|
| Can you download? | ✔ Yes, in app |
| Per-device monthly quota | ❌ No; it’s total titles |
| Total titles allowed at once | ~15–25 across all devices |
| Max devices for downloads | ~2 at the same time |
| Laptop downloads? | ✔ In supported app |
| Reset time | ❌ No monthly reset like Netflix; clear old downloads |

---

If you tell me **which device(s)** you want to use (phone, tablet, laptop), I can give **exact steps** to maximize your download storage and avoid hitting the limits again!
